title: Giants’ Calvin Austin III carted off field following knee injury
content:
Veteran wide receiver Calvin Austin III was carted off New York Giants practice on Tuesday after suffering what appeared to be a significant right knee injury while running a route during one-on-one drills. Austin appeared to be clutching at his right knee while on the ground, clearly in a lot of pain. While the specifics of his injury are currently unknown, his teammates’ reaction was telling. All of the wide receivers and defensive backs couldn’t even look as trainers attended to Austin.

The rest of the team, which was at the other end of the field doing another drill, came down to wish Austin well before he was carted off. The receivers and defensive backs held a lengthy prayer circle until practice resumed.

Austin, who signed a one-year $1.5 million deal in free agency with New York, was expected to start in the slot for the Giants and has made a good impression on coach John Harbaugh during training camp and the preseason.

“It’s pretty clear all the things he does well, ” Harbaugh said Monday. “And the nice thing about Calvin is that he can play all three spots. You can move him around in any one of those positions. He’s a quote, unquote, smaller receiver, and yet he can go outside. He’s played outside a lot. You don’t see that that often. So, he gives us a lot of versatility that way. … Everything you ask him to do, he does it well. He’s very reliable. Runs the right routes, makes catches. He’s been that way his whole career.”

Austin, a fourth-round pick of the Steelers in 2022, spent four years in Pittsburgh before joining the Giants in free agency. He hauled in 31 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns last season. His best season came in 2024, when he caught 36 passes for 548 yards and four scores.

If Austin is indeed out for a significant length of time, it could have big ramifications on the Giants’ depth chart, especially with cut day looming this Sunday.

Fellow veterans Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios could be called upon to replace Austin in the slot. The Giants, of course, also have Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields on the depth chart, with deep threat Darius Slayton still in the mix.

However, one of the big questions on Giants fans’ minds following Austin’s injury is whether that will create a roster spot for the Giants to keep fan-favorite Odell Beckham Jr. Earlier this week, we projected a 53-man roster that did not include Beckham. However, we did have Austin making the initial cut, so if Austin’s injury is significant, perhaps Beckham would have a better chance of securing a spot on the Week 1 roster.

Beckham, who has had a lackluster camp and preseason, is competing with fellow receivers Isaiah Hodgins, Beaux Collins, Dalen Cambre, Jalin Hyatt, Xavier Gipson and Ryan Miller, as well as roster-bubble players at other positions.
